description: Severity distribution for falls from height, unmitigated (no PPE, nets, or barriers). P(death) scale from AIS mortality data.
assumptions: Hard landing surface (concrete/steel) — default worst-case receiving environment
Unmitigated: no engineered controls (harness, net, guardrail)
metalog_note: P(death) is bounded [0,1]. Use Bounds::Bounded(0.0, 1.0) for metalog fitting. Quantile values at exact boundaries (0.0, 1.0) are stored as 0.0001 and 0.999 for logit transform compatibility.

magnitude_bands.description: Standing height / same level. Trip, slip, stumble with fall to ground.
magnitude_bands.rationale: Most same-level falls produce minor or no injury. P90 reflects fracture risk from awkward landing (wrist, ankle). Working-age adults rarely die from standing-height falls.

magnitude_bands.description: Low elevation. Ladders, loading docks, low platforms, vehicles.
magnitude_bands.mortality_source: Lapostolle 2005, Liu 2009; 1-4% mortality in trauma registries
magnitude_bands.rationale: Median outcome is moderate injury (fractures, sprains needing treatment). P90 reflects head-first impact onto concrete — serious but usually survivable. Crosses SIF threshold at P90.

magnitude_bands.description: Medium elevation. Scaffolding, roofs, mezzanines, first/second floor.
magnitude_bands.rationale: Median outcome is serious injury (displaced fractures, spinal injury, organ damage). P90 = fatality reflects head/spine-first impact. 3m is the height at which AIS >= 3 becomes the majority outcome. This is unambiguously SIF territory.

magnitude_bands.description: High elevation. Multi-storey structures, towers, cranes (low), tall scaffolding.
magnitude_bands.rationale: P10=0.01 reflects best-case feet-first landing producing a moderate fracture. Median is serious injury. P90=fatality from head/spine-first impact. Published mortality 10-25% for this range.

magnitude_bands.description: Very high elevation. Multi-storey buildings, industrial structures, tall cranes.
magnitude_bands.mortality_source: LD50 at ~12-15m across multiple studies; 25-75% mortality across this range
magnitude_bands.rationale: This band contains LD50 (~12-15m). P50=0.50 reflects the ~50% mortality midpoint. P10=serious_injury for survivors with polytrauma. P90=fatality for the majority of upper-band impacts.

magnitude_bands.description: Extreme elevation. High-rise, telecommunications towers, bridges.
magnitude_bands.mortality_source: 75-90%+ mortality above 20m; survival is the exception (case reports)
magnitude_bands.rationale: Near-certain fatality at any body orientation on any surface. Rare survivors have extreme polytrauma. The distribution collapses to a near-point-mass at P(death) ≈ 1.0.

surface.description: Multiplier on P(death). Default calibration assumes concrete/steel (1.0). Soft ground roughly halves mortality. Safety net reduces by ~95% (ANSI Z359.2 test data).

age.description: Multiplier on P(death). Default calibration assumes working-age (18-65). Elderly have ~2-3x higher mortality at any height due to osteoporosis, anticoagulants, reduced physiological reserve.

sources.author: Lau et al.
sources.relevance: 1,579 fall patients, height vs ISS/mortality. Key dose-response source.

sources.author: Lapostolle et al.
sources.relevance: Prospective study identifying 6m as critical threshold for major trauma.

sources.author: Liu et al.
sources.relevance: Trauma registry fall analysis, height-mortality relationship.

sources.author: Dickinson et al.
sources.relevance: Falls from height in trauma registries, AIS distribution by height.

sources.author: Baker et al.
sources.relevance: AIS mortality rates (ISS basis). Foundation for P(death) scale.

sources.author: OSHA
sources.relevance: Fatal Four analysis: falls = 36.4% of construction fatalities. 6ft (1.83m) threshold.

sources.author: HSE
sources.relevance: Work at Height Regulations 2005. 2m threshold. Falls = #1 cause of workplace death in UK.

validation_notes: STKY check: 6m fall onto concrete should give P(SIF) > 0.50 — medium band P50 = 0.10 (serious_injury), meets SIF threshold ✓
STKY check: 10m fall should give P(SIF) > 0.80 — high band, nearly all outcomes are serious+ ✓

Cross-check: OSHA ITA 2024 has 10,576 fall-to-lower-level events with 13 fatalities. At reported heights (mostly 2-6m), 0.12% fatality rate is consistent with low-medium band mortality after accounting for survivorship bias in reporting.
The P10/P50/P90 quantiles are set on the P(death) scale, not the ordinal severity scale. They feed directly into metalog SPT fitting.
